note: 25 pages, 40 measured regions on 19 pages: 14 figure rows, 3 table rows and 23 refusals. Eighteen caption lines print as sixteen designators - every body figure is misspelled "Figue N", Figure 4 prints twice on two pages, and Table 3 plus the Table 1 spill own no measured region.
rules: Forty measured regions on nineteen of the twenty-five pages resolve into fourteen figure rows, three table rows and twenty-three refusals, with no region left over [caption.numbering].

Eighteen caption lines print, but only sixteen distinct designators: every body figure caption is spelled "Figue N:" with the r missing - Figue 1 to Figue 11 - while Figures 12 and 13 on p20 are spelled correctly. A designator scan for "Figure\s*\d" therefore finds two of the eighteen captions and reports the other sixteen pages as uncaptioned [caption.numbering].

Figure 4 prints twice, on facing pages and with different art: "Figue 4: Basic information of the three major forest species" over the p7 region and "Figue 4: Whole process forest wood" over the p8 region. Both are recorded as separate rows sharing one printed number, so eighteen caption lines carry sixteen numbers [caption.numbering].

Table 3 prints its caption and its grid but owns no measured region. The caption sits at p13 y 386.5 and the five-column grid prints from y 402.2 to y 530.5, drawn as per-column rule segments 83.5 to 94.8 pt wide with no full-width rule anywhere. The rule detector needs one segment wider than its threshold - Table 4 on p19 qualifies at 141.8 pt, Table 3 does not at 94.8 - so the grid never becomes a region and Table 3 is declared rather than guessed [caption.numbering].

Table 1 spills onto the next page: seven more notation rows print at the top of p5 under a single bottom rule at y 192.6, with cell fills but no header and no caption, and that half owns no measured region either. The recorded row is the four rows under the caption, and continued is false because nothing on p5 is a region [table.continued].

Citation is thinner than in any paper in this block: three numbered references in the body - "listed in Table 1" on p4, "shown in Fig 6" on p11, and "the red dotted line in Fig. 10" on p16, the last printing a page BEFORE its art. Eleven more pointers are deictic and numberless: "as shown in the following Table", "shown in Fig." with the number missing, "the following figure", "the above figure", "the blue area of the figure", "the analysis of the figure" [mention.count].

The Figure 6 caption is split across the full page width - "Figue 6: Carbon sequestration levels of forest trees under different" at x 99.9 with "values" at x 457.5 on the same baseline - and the Figure 5 caption stops mid-phrase at "under three values of" with nothing printed after it on either page [caption.verbatim].

Figure 13 prints its caption inside its own measured box: the art occupies the top of the region and the caption baseline sits at y 756.0 against a region bottom of y 769.9, the only row in the paper whose caption is inside the region rather than below it [caption.position].

Twenty-five display equations are numbered (1) to (25) in the right margin but only seventeen regions hold one: on p12, equations 6 and 11 own boxes while 7, 8, 9 and 10 are typeset inline. The boxes carry no text layer at all, so a region with zero words and 16 to 94 paths in a body column is an equation, never an exhibit [geometry.family].

The appendix reprints a science article whose own figures carry "Fig. 1" on p23 and "Fig. 2" on p24. Those belong to the article, not to the paper, and are refused. The p24 art is the same 1.9 MB embedded chart form as Figure 5 on p10 and holds 7373 paths, but the layout pass emits no region on that page at all, so the article page is declared unmeasured rather than counted [caption.numbering].

The chart forms paste their data points as sub-point circles that the viewer does not paint: Figure 5 holds 7202 0.79 pt filled circles and Figure 8 holds 1000, and at 600 dpi none of them draw a single pixel, so both figures print as axes, callouts and legends around an empty plot. The rows are recorded from what the page actually shows, with the missing series named in the note [geometry.family].
